name: get_question_answer
description: Collect the user's answer to a question you asked with ask_user_question when that call returned pending: true because the user had not answered yet. Waits for the answer, up to this call's limit, and returns it. If the user still has not answered, it returns pending: true again: call it again with the same question_id. Do not ask the question again, and do not message the user while you wait.

question_id.description: The question_id from the pending ask_user_question result.

name: image_generate
description: Generate an image, or edit and restyle existing images given as reference_images, with the image service the user configured in Codeg, and save it as a file. Use it when the task needs a raster image (an illustration, photo, icon, texture, banner, mockup); draw things better made in code (SVG icons, charts, CSS) in code instead. Write a detailed prompt: the subject, style, composition, colors, lighting, and any text to render, quoted exactly. The image is written to output_path when you give one (a relative path is resolved against the session's working directory; a directory, or a path without an extension, gets a generated file name; an existing file is replaced). Without output_path it goes to Codeg's image folder: copy or move it into the project yourself if it belongs there. Generating takes from a few seconds to a couple of minutes. If it is not done when this call returns, the result says so and gives a job_id: call image_get_result with it to wait, and do not start the same image again. A finished result gives the saved file's absolute path and pixel size, and a small preview of the image when the user allows it.

prompt.description: What to draw, or what to change in the reference images.

model.description: Model to use. Omit to use the user's default.

aspect_ratio.description: Shape of the image. Omit for the service default (usually square).

resolution.description: Size class of the longer edge. Omit for about 1K. Larger is slower and costs more.

size.description: Exact WIDTHxHEIGHT in pixels, for GPT image models (for example 1536x1024). Takes precedence over aspect_ratio and resolution where the model accepts it.

quality.description: Rendering quality, for models that support it (GPT image models). Lower is faster and cheaper.

background.description: transparent needs a model that supports it (GPT image models) and a .png or .webp output_path.

reference_images.description: Local image files (absolute, or relative to the working directory) to edit, or to use as references. Say in the prompt what to do with them.

output_path.description: Where to save the image. The extension (.png, .jpg, .webp) picks the format.

name: image_get_result
description: Wait for images started by image_generate and collect them, by job_id. Returns as soon as one of them finishes, or when this call's wait ends; call again with the ones still running. A finished job gives the saved file's absolute path and pixel size, and a small preview of the image when the user allows it. While you are only waiting, do not message the user about it; just call again.

name: create_assistant
description: Save a new assistant for the user: a named, @-mentionable delegation preset in Codeg — an agent, every one of its options picked (model, effort, mode…), and standing instructions handed to that agent with every task delegated to it. Use it when the user asks to add, create or set up an assistant ("add a reviewer assistant on Codex with high effort", "make me an @translator"). Do NOT use it to get work done now — that is delegate_to_agent — and do not create one the user did not ask for. Name only the options the user mentioned: Codeg reads the agent's real option list (it launches the agent briefly, which can take a few seconds) and leaves everything else at the agent's own defaults. The reply says what was saved, which options kept their defaults, and the assistant_id; the user can then @-mention it anywhere, and you can delegate to it with delegate_to_agent's assistant_id. The user sees the new assistant in this conversation and can edit or delete it there or in Settings.

name.description: What the user @-mentions it by, up to 40 characters, unique among their assistants, e.g. "Reviewer".

agent_type.description: The agent it runs on, as a Codeg agent slug ("claude_code", "codex", "gemini", "open_code", "deepseek", …) or the agent's name ("Codex CLI"). It must be installed and switched on in Codeg.

description.description: One line on when to use it, up to 200 characters. Shown in the mention list, and it tells a delegating agent when to pick this assistant.

instructions.description: Standing instructions: the role and the working rules the agent gets with every task delegated to it, written to that agent ("You review diffs… Lead with the verdict…"). Up to 20,000 characters. Do not put a specific task here.

model.description: The model the assistant runs, by its id or the name the agent shows (e.g. "gpt-5.5" or "GPT-5.5"). Omit to keep the agent's default model (or, in an update, the assistant's current one). If the agent has no such model, nothing is saved and the reply lists the models it offers.

mode.description: The agent's mode or approval preset, by id or name (e.g. "read-only", "Plan"). Omit for the default (or the current one in an update).

option.description: The option's id or the name the agent shows, e.g. "reasoning_effort" or "Fast mode".

value.description: The value's id or name, e.g. "high"; for an on/off option, "true" or "false".

options.description: Any other agent option, one {option, value} pair each, both by id or by the name the agent shows: [{"option": "reasoning_effort", "value": "high"}, {"option": "Fast mode", "value": "true"}]. Only the options the user asked for: every option left out keeps the agent's default (or the assistant's current pick in an update). An option or value the agent does not offer is refused with the list of what it does offer.

avatar_emoji.description: Optional: one emoji for its avatar. Omit for a monogram of its name.

avatar_color.description: Optional: the avatar's colour. Omit for one derived from the name.

enabled.description: Whether it can be delegated to right away. Defaults to true.

name: update_assistant
description: Change one of the user's existing assistants — its name, description, instructions, agent, model or other options, avatar, or whether it is switched on — when the user asks to ("switch the reviewer to GPT-5.4", "make @translator also keep code blocks as they are"). Pass only what should change; everything else stays as it is, including every option you do not name. Changing the agent, model, mode or options makes Codeg read the agent's option list again, which can take a few seconds. To rewrite instructions, pass the complete new text: it replaces the old one. The reply says what changed.

assistant.description: Which assistant: its assistant_id (e.g. "7" — from a codeg://assistant/<id> link in the user's message, the delegate_to_agent roster, or create_assistant's reply) or its exact name.

name.description: A new name, up to 40 characters, unique among the user's assistants.

description.description: A new one-line description (an empty string clears it).

instructions.description: The complete new standing instructions; they replace the old ones.

agent_type.description: Move it to another agent (slug or name). Its options are then picked anew for that agent: the ones you name, the agent's defaults for the rest.

model.description: The model the assistant runs, by its id or the name the agent shows (e.g. "gpt-5.5" or "GPT-5.5"). Omit to keep the agent's default model (or, in an update, the assistant's current one). If the agent has no such model, nothing is saved and the reply lists the models it offers.

mode.description: The agent's mode or approval preset, by id or name (e.g. "read-only", "Plan"). Omit for the default (or the current one in an update).

option.description: The option's id or the name the agent shows, e.g. "reasoning_effort" or "Fast mode".

value.description: The value's id or name, e.g. "high"; for an on/off option, "true" or "false".

options.description: Any other agent option, one {option, value} pair each, both by id or by the name the agent shows: [{"option": "reasoning_effort", "value": "high"}, {"option": "Fast mode", "value": "true"}]. Only the options the user asked for: every option left out keeps the agent's default (or the assistant's current pick in an update). An option or value the agent does not offer is refused with the list of what it does offer.

avatar_emoji.description: A new avatar emoji; an empty string goes back to the name's monogram.

enabled.description: Switch it on (true) or off (false); a switched-off assistant cannot be delegated to.

name: continue_delegation
description: Give a delegated task that has FINISHED (completed, failed or canceled) more work in the SAME sub-agent session: the sub-agent keeps everything it read and did, its working directory or worktree, and its model and options, and gets your new instructions as a follow-up. Use it to iterate on a result — fix what it got wrong, extend it, apply review feedback — instead of starting a cold delegate_to_agent that would redo the context. It returns a NEW task_id for this round right away and runs in the background like any delegation; its result comes back the same way. Only the LATEST round of a task can be continued (a continued round is refused with not_latest_round and the id to use), never one still running (task_running: wait for it, or cancel it first). If the sub-agent's session cannot be loaded again it is refused with session_unavailable rather than started empty — delegate a new task then. To pick an INTERRUPTED task back up without new instructions, use resume_delegation instead.

task_id.description: The task to continue: the task_id of its latest round (from delegate_to_agent, or from a previous continue_delegation).

task.description: The follow-up instructions. The sub-agent remembers the task so far, so say only what to do next.
